text:
[LLOG.15.3] **A rule ends a justification it depends on only by a flip the
cycle check refutes.** A logical fact is retracted when its last justifier's
match ends ([LLOG.15.1]). A rule that reads the logical fact and ends that
match has an edge back into the justifying rule unless the check drops it:

- **An emit the literal break refutes compiles,** unless it replaces a fact
  the rule itself matched, which [LLOG.11.9] refuses. It cannot trigger the justifier, so the edge drops ([LCYC.6.1]). What
  its firing leaves is [LLOG.15.1]'s, and the rule reads the fact whose
  justification it ends.
- **Any other way of ending the match is refused.** A `withdraw` of the fact
  the justifier matches ([LCYC.3.2.2]), or an emit whose value the break cannot
  compare, keeps the edge. Both rules are then in one SCC with the logical fact
  emitted and matched inside it, and the compiler refuses the program with
  `DS_VALIDATE_RULE_CYCLE` ([LCYC.3.1.1]). Truth maintenance earns no exception:
  that the retraction would end the loop is not an argument the cycle check
  takes ([LCYC.3.5.1]).

A refused program, and a transition that must outlast the rule that makes it,
have two shapes that compile. **A state that holds exactly
while a condition holds is itself a logical fact**: emitted `logical` from the
condition, it is retracted when the condition stops matching, and no rule
turns it off. **A transition no condition justifies enters from outside the
engine**: the host or an adapter asserts the changed fact, which is no edge of
the rule graph, and the cascade follows it as it follows any input. A loop
closed through an adapter is the adapter's to keep finite ([LCYC.7.1]).
